messages:
alex: quick sync: thinking about extracting 'model-adapters' into a plugin boundary to decouple runtime from model-specific code. thoughts?

maya: +1. current coupling causes changes to runtime whenever we onboard a new model variant.

sam: what's the proposed surface? small interface that exposes load(), infer(request), cleanup()? also version pinning?

priya: two-phase approach: 1) adapter facade inside runtime; 2) move adapters to separate process/plugins with a clear contract. dogfood internally before full split.

dave: Operational concerns: plugin lifecycle, metrics, per-plugin resource limits. If we allow third-party plugins we need sandboxing.

alex: Agreed. Plan: start with 'in-process plugin' model (shared lib) with strict API and semver. After 2 months evaluate runtime perf and deploy complexity. If ok, iterate to process-isolated plugin containers. Rollback: feature flag to route back to builtin adapters.

maya: How about KV cache ownership? Adapters shouldn't own global cache. Suggest exposing cache API from runtime instead of allowing direct access. :thinking:

sam: ```go
type Adapter interface {
  Init(config json.RawMessage) error
  Infer(input *InferenceRequest) (*InferenceResponse, error)
  Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error
}
```

priya: Testing: add adapter conformance tests (unit + integration) and an adapter fuzzer to catch API drift.

dave: We also need observability: per-adapter request counts, latency p50/p95, error rate, token counts. Add tags: adapter_name, model_variant.

maya: Who'll own migration? I'd propose Infra + Eng-Runtime pair for first 2 sprints, then handover to owners (eng-platform) for ops runbook.

alex: I'll draft an RFC with phases, compatibility promises, and rollout checklist. tagging @maya @sam @pri for review. ETA: draft by next Tue.

infra-bot: RFC created: https://rwd.infra/rfcs/1823-plugin-adapters. Assigned reviewers: alex, maya, sam. :white_check_mark:

sam: :thumbsup: one more ask — include benchmark targets (latency overhead <2ms p50, <5ms p95) and a regression test.

alex: Noted. Will include perf targets and migration runbook. Thanks!
